# Step 2.70 — Save a copy and upload it

## Builder 1 (file format, saving on the tracker, server side of the upload)

**What exists.** `packages/contracts/src/game-copy.ts`: `writeGameCopy` / `readGameCopy` (refusal codes `not-a-copy`, `damaged`, `unknown-version`, `other-league`, `other-game`), the upload's body `GameCopyUpload` (`{ copy: <file text>, takeOver?: { expectedHolderSince } }`), its reply `GameCopyUploadReply` (`uploaded {added, alreadyThere, notTaken}`, `held-by-other {holder, sentAt}`, `refused {code}`) and `gameCopyRefusalStatus`. The file holds league, game, `savedAt` and each command with its ID and protocol version; no account, session or device. The commands hold player IDs, jersey numbers, tap times, and the name typed for a player added at the scorer's table (nothing else about a person). On the tracker: `game-copy-on-device.ts` (pure: what goes in, file name, `suggestsCopy`), `save-copy-parts.tsx` (`SaveCopy` behind More, `SaveCopySuggestion` beside the notices after `offlineLongMs`, five minutes, with plays waiting). Wired in `tracker-opening.tsx` only (the `slots.more` prop and one line in the notices); `tracker-controller.ts` is untouched. Server: `apps/web/src/server/game-copy-upload-endpoint.ts` and the route `POST /api/v1/leagues/{leagueId}/games/{game}/copy` (body up to 4 MB, `jsonBody` takes a limit now). `replyOf` in `scoring-session-endpoint.ts` is exported; `SessionHolder` is exported from the contracts. Messages: `tracker.copy.*` in `packages/site/src/messages/en/tracker.ts`, including the words for every refusal code (`tracker.copy.refused.<code>`). Decisions T-360 to T-364 (pending files), T6 §4 corrected. No new core command or read, so no role-matrix row; the upload runs `openScoringSession`, `takeOverScoring`, `releaseScoringSession`, `readTrackerState` and the door's `applyTrackerCommands`, all `games.score`.

**How the upload works (T-361).** It asks the door first under a session that holds nothing (saves nothing; answers `duplicate` for what the server has). Nothing new: answered at once, the game not touched. Otherwise it opens the game as the tracker does, on a fresh device id of its own; another device holding it is answered `held-by-other`, and the page must ask the takeover question and post again with `takeOver.expectedHolderSince = holder.since`. Then the new commands go in batches under that session, which is released at the end. Final or called off: `reopen-first` (409).

**What passed.** Unit tests: `packages/contracts/src/game-copy.test.ts` (7), `apps/web/src/features/tracker/game-copy-on-device.test.ts` (4), `apps/web/src/server/game-copy-upload-endpoint.test.ts` (8: copy first then tablet late, tablet first then copy, half and half, takeover asked, uploaded twice, not allowed and visitor, final game, wrong game and damaged). The 8 were seen failing first against a stub. `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `packages/site` tests, `tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs`; the tracker, server and contracts folders as the report says.

**What builder 2 builds.**

- The upload page under `apps/web/src/app/[league]/score/` (for instance `[game]/upload/page.tsx`), linked with the address helper (`leagueUrl`, add a page name if needed), never a hand-written `/{league}/` address. Signed in and allowed to score, as the tracker page is (T-258); reads the file in the browser (`<input type="file">`, `file.text()`), posts `{ copy }` with `Content-Type: application/json` to the route, shows `uploaded` counts, asks the takeover question on `held-by-other` (who, when last heard; reuse the tracker's takeover words) and posts again with `takeOver`, and words every refusal with `tracker.copy.refused.<code>`. All other text in message files.
- A way to the page: from "Your games", the tracker's More (beside Save a copy) or both; say which.
- The pinned lists of rule 9: page-step rows in `scripts/check-web-shell.mjs`, the harmful-text test's page route and file field (the copy route is already in its `ANSWERS`, as `[keeper, owner]`; check it answers there, it has POST only), `unreleased-page.test.ts`, `adminPlaceholders` in `nothing-unfinished-test.mjs`, `activity-messages.test.ts` if a read is added.
- A browser test `tests/browser/save-copy-test.mjs`: score offline on one device, Save a copy (catch the download), upload it signed in on another context, one result; the first device then sends late and nothing counts twice; a person who may not score is refused; the five-minute suggestion shows (the controller's clock can be moved as the sleep tests do).

**What I distrust.** A copy uploaded after another device re-entered the same plays by hand counts them twice (they have new IDs); the takeover question is the only guard. Plays the first device makes after the upload took its game are listed not saved, and "Send these plays" then refuses them `game-moved`, so they are entered again. The download on iPhone Safari is not tried in a browser yet. The probe and the sends are separate transactions: a device taking the game between them makes the rest `notTaken`, never counted twice.

## Builder 2 (the upload page, its links, its checks)

**What exists.** The page `/{league}/score/{game}/upload` (`app/[league]/score/[game]/upload/page.tsx` → `features/tracker/upload-copy-page.tsx`), built by the address helper as the new league page `score-upload` (`league-url.ts`, released in `server/releases.ts`). The server checks it as the tracker page does (league gate with sign-in and back, `readTrackerRosters` for `mayScoreGame`); a game recorded as a final score or box score is told where its score goes; a final live game gets the form and the server's "reopen it first". It is not a tracker address, so it sits in the league's frame and the worker never keeps it. The form (`upload-copy-form.tsx`, client) reads the file with `file.text()`, posts `{ copy }` to the copy route (`leagueApiUrl`), and shows: the counts (`uploadedLines`: new, already there, not taken), each refusal as `tracker.copy.refused.<code>` (401 signed out, 403 and 404 of the league's own gate mapped too), and on `held-by-other` the tracker's own takeover words (`heldByOther`, `LastHeard`, `takeOverQuestionText`, Yes/Not now); Yes posts again with `takeOver.expectedHolderSince = holder.since`. The pure part is `upload-copy.ts` (+ test, 4). The page counts its answers (`data-upload-answers`) so a test never reads the answer before. Messages `tracker.upload.*` and `tracker.copy.where`.

**Links (S-97, pending, Decided for you).** Each game in "Your games" (`my-games-page.tsx`, beside "Score this game") and "Save a copy" behind More and in the suggestion (`save-copy-parts.tsx`, new tab, so the game is never left). `uploadHref` is a new prop of `TrackerOpening`, given by `tracker-page.tsx`. `tracker-controller.ts` and `tracker-route-test` untouched. P7 §5.2 corrected.

**Pinned lists.** `check-web-shell.mjs`: the page for every kind of person (owner, scheduler, scorekeeper 200; coach, team coach, stranger, the draft league's five staff roles and another league's admin 403; visitor 307 to sign in and back; no such game and another league's 404) and the link in "Your games". Harmful text: the page route in `ROUTES` (its one field is a file, no plain form). `HELPERS` unchanged (no helper added; the chain finds a test by its file, so `game-copy-test` is in it with no list edited). No admin page, read, command, table or migration: the other lists of rule 9 do not apply.

**What passed.** `tests/browser/game-copy-test.mjs`, 19 checks: A scores offline, Save a copy (download caught: 3 plays, this game); the owner uploads from another context; the takeover question names A, "Not now" sends nothing, "Yes" uploads 3 new and each play is on the server once; the same file again adds 0 (3 already there); A back online, opened again, sends late and the server still has each play once, A's screen 6–3; a coach and a person with no role get 403 and no file field; signed out goes to sign in and back; the game ended, a copy with new command IDs is refused "This game has ended. Reopen it first…", nothing counted. `harmful-text-test` passed (2167 checks, 41 page routes, 21 answer routes). `npm run test:web` 288 checks. Vitest: tracker, unreleased, releases, leagues rules, site, pending decisions (1195). `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`.

**What I distrust / left.** After the upload lets go of the game, A is told "This device has left the game" (not "taken over") with no list of its plays; they are sent only once A opens the game again. Sound (nothing counted twice) but a scorekeeper may not know the plays still wait: worth a word on that screen (product, not this step's files). The five-minute suggestion is not in the browser test (builder 1's note asked for it; the lead's brief did not). The download on iPhone Safari is still untried.

## Independent review (not the builder; fixed nothing)

Attacks run as a throwaway vitest file beside `game-copy-upload-endpoint.test.ts` (deleted), with `openScoringSession` and `releaseScoringSession` wrapped to act in the gaps.

**High.** A play made on the tablet after its copy was saved is lost to the server once an upload took the game: the tablet's next send is refused `session-not-held` (reason `released`, since the upload let go: "This device has left the game"), and "Send these plays" is refused `game-moved`, whether the uploader was the same scorekeeper or the owner. Reproduce: tablet opens, 4 plays copied, a fifth made after; upload with takeover yes; the tablet sends `[p5]` with `notSavedSince: 0` → `game-moved`. The plays are listed not saved, so nothing counts twice, but every play since the save must be entered again by hand, on a screen that says only "Open it again" (builder 1 named it; builder 2's note judged it "sound": it is sound only for plays inside the copy). Cause: `game-moved-since.ts:52` counts the uploaded events as another's (wrong account, or IDs not in the batch, since `dropTaken` removed them). Smallest fix: the tracker keeps its own taken command IDs in the "Send these plays" batch (they answer `duplicate` and join `own`; tried: same scorekeeper then accepted, sequence 5), and `gameMovedSince` treats an event whose ID is in `own` as own whatever account recorded it (needed when the owner uploaded). The browser test never makes a play after the save, so it cannot see this.

**Medium.** If the release at `game-copy-upload-endpoint.ts:232` fails, the route answers 500 though the plays were saved (and `afterwards` never publishes them to watchers); the game stays held by the upload's own device (`copy-upload-…`) until its lease ends, so the tablet is asked the takeover question naming its own scorekeeper. Nothing counted twice: uploading again answered 0 added, 4 already there.

**Low.** (a) A file over 2,000,000 characters (a 100,000-command copy is 3.5 MB) is answered 400 `invalid-input`, which the page words as a general failure (`upload-copy.ts:70`); the form reads any file whole (`file.text()`) with no size check first. (b) The copy holds only the plays still waiting (T-363), not "the game's commands" as the plan line says: it is not a backup of the whole game; the plan wording should follow T-363. (c) The filter at `game-copy-upload-endpoint.ts:197` is caught by one test only ("the tablet first, the copy late"); "uploaded twice" still passes without it.

**Holds.** (1) The tablet sending 3 of 4 plays between the probe and the take (takeover yes): 1 added, 3 already there, then the tablet's late send all `duplicate`, sequence 4; the door checks `takenCommands` under the game's lock. (2) League and person come from the session and address: another league's game ID at this league's address 404; the file's league or game edited → `other-league`/`other-game`; edited to match, its commands become this game's plays by this person, as a tracker post would. The batch is built by the endpoint, so a file cannot set `withoutMercyOrLastMinutes`, `notSavedSince` or `accountId`; inside a command it is `damaged`. (3) Coach, stranger, another league's admin 403 at the POST; visitor 401; scheduler and owner allowed; the same `mayScoreGame` as the door. (4) 100,000 commands, 999,000-deep JSON as the file, 400,000-deep inside a command, `savedAt` as a string: each refused, no crash. The name typed for a player is not shown by the upload page (counts only) and is rendered by React elsewhere (by reading). (5) Final: `game-closed` → 409 before anything is sent; final between take and send is answered by the door's `isPlayable` under the lock → `notTaken`. (6) Broken by hand: skip the "already has" filter → "the tablet first, the copy late" failed; drop the `other-game` check in `game-copy.ts:127` → the contracts test and the endpoint's "copy of another game" failed. The browser test's `step` catches add to `failures`, which exits 1; nothing passes on a timeout.
